closed_world.value: Post-hurricane New Orleans and surrounding Louisiana during disaster cleanup operations
closed_world.quote: Houses torn from foundations, boats in the streets, abandoned cars everywhere, no power, no sewer, no drinking water.

investigator.value: First-person narrator—a former prison inmate and enforcer with violent history who arrives in New Orleans post-hurricane
investigator.quote: I went to the private prison in Shelby and made my way to Deer Lodge... I left when they told me to leave.

suspect_architecture.value: No traditional suspect architecture present. The narrator is the acknowledged killer of five men who attacked his brother; no investigative whodunit structure exists. The five victims are undifferentiated as a group.
suspect_architecture.quote: five men tried to kill my younger brother over some logging rights money

red_herring.value: The forensic framing around the shootings functions as institutional misdirection: three deaths ruled hunting accidents, two ruled impossible at their range — the court's own expert inadvertently provides cover for the narrator's skill.
red_herring.quote: No bullet could be accurate, at that range. That's what the forensic expert said.

clue_fairness.value: No fair-play clue structure is present. This is a confessional first-person noir narrative, not a puzzle mystery; the narrator reveals his own guilt directly rather than through planted clues available to a reader-investigator.

social_world.value: Interlocking hierarchies of frontier criminality, debt networks, prison economy, and disaster capitalism: men who owe favors, contract killers, private prisons, and hurricane cleanup contractors exploiting displaced Gulf Coast poor.
social_world.quote: guys who owed me favors, guys who sometimes paid me to move the index finger of my right hand less than an inch

alibi.value: The narrator's effective alibi is geographic and physical impossibility: shots fired at ranges the court forensic expert deemed impossible, laundered as hunting accidents, distributing culpability into statistical improbability.
alibi.quote: The other two were shot at distances that were deemed impossible by the court forensic expert.

reveal_mechanic.value: No formal reveal mechanic exists. The story operates as sustained confession rather than mystery resolution; the narrator self-discloses culpability throughout without an external investigator or dramatic unmasking.

media_and_audience.value: The hurricane disaster functions as macro-level media spectacle that obscures individual crime: the court proceedings, Montana state police questions, and the overwhelmed post-Katrina institutional chaos all absorb and neutralize accountability.
media_and_audience.quote: Montana state police questions about five men and their sudden death with my name as the answer

investigator_wound.value: The narrator is simultaneously perpetrator and self-investigator; his wound is moral dissociation — eight years of prison and biblical vengeance theology have severed his sense of reality, leaving him unable to feel the world as real.
investigator_wound.quote: Things didn't seem real to me anymore. My brother met me at my release, eight years and he was doing well
